messages:
sarah: ok team, handing off night anchor - I'm the outgoing primary. quick recap: earlier today we saw a customer-facing latency spike on /v1/generate between 18:12-18:47 UTC that affected ~4% of requests. oncall-bot posted the incident bridge and we escalated to infra; mitigation (temporary routing to smaller model pool + cache purge) reduced errors. leaving detailed notes below, and verifying access before I sign off.

oncall-bot: INCIDENT STARTED 2024-10-12T18:12:03Z | #incident-1932 | latency-spike | impact: partial customer latency | assigned: sarah, mike | bridge: https://meet.example/incident-1932 :rotating_light:

sarah: immediate actions taken: 1) rolled routing rule to fallback-model-a (see runbook link) 2) purged prefix cache for high-traffic keyspace 3) raised autoscaler min for the small pool to avoid cold-starts. no data exfil; customer requests were retried gracefully.

jordan: thanks for the handoff notes. are all the temp rules still active? I can keep primary if you need extra time.

sarah: jordan - yes, temp rules are active. exact commands I ran:
```
# routing change
redwoodctl route set --route /v1/generate --model fallback-model-a --policy fallback
# cache purge for prefix k:session:
redwoodctl cache purge --prefix "k:session:"
```
I left the traffic cap at 60% on fallback-model-a. autoscaler bump: `rconfig set pool-small.autoscale.min 3`

mike: quick perms check before you go — can you confirm everyone has PD & access to grafana dashboard we use? I couldn't see some graphs earlier.

sarah: mike, I verified PD schedules: @maria was on rotation earlier but we changed to you/jordan nights. PagerDuty service is `redwood-inference-prod`; make sure you have `Responder` on that service. Grafana: dashboard `infra/latency/v1-generate` is team-shared, but there's a second org-level dashboard we use for billing that requires `grafana-admin` or team view.

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty check: user mike - Responder (OK), user jordan - Responder (OK), user ana - Not assigned to redwood-inference-prod.

ana: hey, adding myself as secondary now. I did not have PD access earlier — requesting assignment.

mike: ack. sarah, can you drop the exact runbook links and the short checklist (PD, AWS console role, Grafana)? I want to do the quick preflight.

sarah: runbooks:
- incident runbook: https://docs.example/runbooks/infra/latency-spike
- routing fallback guide: https://docs.example/runbooks/infra/routing-fallbacks
- cache ops: https://docs.example/runbooks/cache/prefix-purge

preflight checklist (copy this when you take over):
- PagerDuty: confirm you can trigger a test page `pd trigger --service redwood-inference-prod --summary "test page"`
- AWS: assume role `arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/OncallAccess` and verify `aws sts get-caller-identity` returns expected account
- Grafana: open `infra/latency/v1-generate` and confirm panels update; test link sharing for the team view
- Runbooks: open the incident runbook and the recent incident notes, ensure you can edit the notes doc

jordan: running PD test now. "pd trigger" returned 200 and routed to my phone. :thumbsup:

mike: AWS role attempt failed for me, getting `AccessDenied` on sts:AssumeRole. I have `dev-team` permission only.

sarah: mike - I added a temporary cross-account role mapping for tonight. try again with `aws sts assume-role --role-arn arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/OncallAccess --role-session-name mike-night`

mike: ok that worked, creds look good. Grafana still shows blank panels for me on the org dashboard, but infra/latency/v1-generate is visible. Maybe need team view permission.

ops-runbooks: Note: If Grafana org-level panels are missing, use the embedded JSON panel link in the runbook to fetch raw metrics `curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer <graf-token>' https://grafana.example/api/datasources/proxy/1/api/v1/query_range?query=latency_query`

mike: got it. i'm toggling alerts threshold back down to normal and leaving routing rule in place. if latency creeps above 400ms for 10m we should automatically roll back fallback rule and open a page.

sarah: one more customer-impact note: partner "WaveApps" saw elevated tail latency and reported two timed-out requests. Support ticket #4451 created. I've added the support contact and the short mitigation msg to the ticket. If it recurs, escalate to the account team.

jordan: coverage gaps — ana is new to PD for this service (just assigned). mike, can you pair with her for 10m so she knows how to run the cache purge and routing rollback steps?

ana: happy to pair now for the cache purge steps.

mike: pairing in 2. also leaving an annotated snippet for quick rollback:
```
# rollback routing
redwoodctl route set --route /v1/generate --model primary-model-v2 --policy default
# restore autoscale
rconfig set pool-small.autoscale.min 1
```

oncall-bot: SHIFT HANDOFF: sarah -> mike (primary) | jordan (secondary) | ana (backup) | checklists signed off: PD test (jordan), AWS assume (mike), Grafana view (mike).

sarah: mike, anything else before I sign out? otherwise i'll sign off at +1m.

mike: all good from me. I'll stay primary for the night. thanks for the thorough notes — super helpful. :bow:
